mechanism.plausibility_rationale: Tendon rupture is not typically associated with the use of penicillin-binding protein inhibitors, such as beta-lactam antibiotics like penicillin. Beta-lactam antibiotics work by inhibiting bacterial cell wall synthesis, which is a process not directly involved in tendon function or integrity. While adverse effects can occur with any medication, tendon rupture is not a known or commonly reported side effect of beta-lactam antibiotics. Therefore, the plausibility of tendon rupture as an adverse effect of this class of antibiotics is considered low.
